name: Philologus
title: Christian in Rome
summary: Philologus was a Christian in Rome whom Paul greeted in his letter to the Romans. He is mentioned together with Julia and other believers, and is thought to have been part of the early Christian community in Rome. Although little is known about him, the mention testifies to his recognition as a faithful member of the fellowship.

keyEvents.title: Greeting from Paul
keyEvents.description: Paul sends a personal greeting to Philologus in his letter to the church in Rome, indicating that he was a known and valued believer.

keyEvents.title: Part of the house church in Rome
keyEvents.description: Philologus is mentioned together with Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, as well as all the saints who were with them, suggesting that they belonged to a house church in Rome.

keyEvents.title: Connection with Julia
keyEvents.description: Philologus is mentioned together with Julia, and many scholars believe they may have been a married couple in the early Christian community in Rome.

keyEvents.title: Part of the broader community of saints
keyEvents.description: Paul refers to 'all the saints who are with them', indicating that Philologos was part of a larger Christian community that met regularly.
